_scope: TWO nodes. Filter New URLs: phase 2 gets a real cap on paid EnrichLayer profiles - the maxEnrich that Expand Phase 2 Queries already records in hhPhase2 (20 for Tier 20, 40 for Tier 40). Phase 1 is unchanged (the tier's maxEnrich, 35 / 55). Expand Phase 2 Queries: COMMENT ONLY - its note that maxEnrich "enforces nothing" becomes false with this change; not one executable line differs (checked by the test). No change to Limit Candidates (left as it is: it cuts nothing either way), the queries, the location/foreign-subdomain rules, the per-search dedupe, scoring or billing.
_why: Found by the independent review of the Tier-40 change and re-verified on production data: the Limit Candidates maxItems expression calls $getWorkflowStaticData, which exists only inside Code nodes, so it resolves to undefined and the limit keeps every item. 27 of 27 retained Limit runs (14 executions, 1913-2048, re-counted 2026-10-01) passed their input through unchanged; phase-2 inputs reached 45 (exec 1913), 36 (2032), 26 (2024, 2039) and 24 (2036) while the recorded phase-2 cap was 20 or 40. (1913 predates the Split-In-Batches reset fix, so its phase 2 was never sent to EnrichLayer; the largest phase 2 actually enriched and paid for is 36, exec 2032 - corrected 2026-10-01 by the post-publish review.) Phase-2 paid enrichment was therefore bounded only by how many profiles phase 2's queries returned - and Stage 2 is about to add queries. The owner ordered this cap before any new query (2026-10-01).
_expectedEffect: The cap does not bind on any retained run: phase 2 sent 9 profiles to EnrichLayer in exec 2048 (Tier 20, cap 20 - the one run under the current page-1-only rules) and 15 in exec 2044 (Tier 40, cap 40, under the PREVIOUS Tier-40 rules with pages 2-5), so no candidate of a recent search would have been cut. It bounds what phase 2 can spend once Stage 2 adds queries: at most 20 profiles (~40 credits) for Tier 20 and 40 (~80 credits) for Tier 40 per search, on top of phase 1's 35 / 55. TRADE-OFF when it does bind: phase 2 enriches at most 20 / 40 profiles, and not every enriched profile qualifies, so a phase 2 that today would enrich more than the cap can deliver fewer candidates than it would uncapped. Evidence that it does not bind today is thin: one run in the current regime (2048) plus the replayed link lists of 2035/2036/2039 (13/12/14 of 20); 2044 predates the Tier-40 change.
_order: When the cap binds, profiles are taken in the order the phase-2 queries were sent: the re-sent queries SerpAPI gave up on first, then the planned queries (bag-of-words, then the no-AND title query, for most titles). If Stage 2 adds queries, their order decides who is enriched first.
